h: The Sabbath Day Meal and Atika Kadisha

p: סְעוּדַת יוֹם שַׁבָּת סְעוּדָתָא דְעַתִּיקָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— The meal of the Sabbath day is the feast of Atika Kadisha, as written in the holy Zohar,
וְהָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה חֲשָׁבָהּ נֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
— and the Ari, of blessed memory, reckoned it corresponding to the holiness of Avraham our Father, peace be upon him;
(וּבִמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לט):
— (and in Midrash Rabbah, Parashah 39):
"'לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶךָ' – לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה אָבִינוּ אַבְרָהָם מִתְפַּחֵד וְאוֹמֵר: תֹּאמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדִי עָוֹן שֶׁהָיִיתִי עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כָּל הַשָּׁנִים?
— “‘To you is the dew of your youth’—because Avraham our Father was afraid and said: Can it be that I bear iniquity for having served idols all those years?
אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶךָ, מָה הַטַּל הַזֶּה פּוֹרֵחַ, אַף עֲוֹנוֹתֶיךָ פּוֹרְחִים,
— The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: 'To you is the dew of your youth; just as this dew dissipates and evaporates, so too your iniquities dissipate;
מָה הַטַּל הַזֶּה סִימָן בְּרָכָה וְכוּלֵי".
— just as this dew is an omen of blessing, etc.'
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מָה תְּשׁוּבָה הֱשִׁיבוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדִּמְיוֹן הַטַּל דַּוְוקָא לְהָנִיחַ דַּעְתּוֹ.
— And one must understand what manner of answer Hashem, blessed be He, answered him through the specific metaphor of dew to set his mind at ease.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 39:8: “Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: “Go you [lekh lekha]” – twice, one from Aram Naharayim and one from Aram Naḥor. Rabbi Neḥemya says: “Lekh lekha” – twice, one from Aram Naharayim and Aram Naḥor, and one when He flew him from [the Covenant] between the Pieces and brought him to Ḥaran. That is what is written: “Your people [amekha] will volunteer on your day of battle [ḥeilekha]” (Psalms 110:3) – I was with you [imekha] when you volunteered on My behalf to descend into the fiery furnace. “On your day of battle” – when you assembled for Me all the hosts [haḥayalot] and masses. “In sacred glory [hadrei]” (Psalms 110:3) – from the radiance [hadar] of the world I sanctified you; “from the womb of the dawn [mishḥar]” (Psalms 110:3) – from the womb of the world I have sought you out [sheḥartikha]. “Yours is the dew of youth” (Psalms 110:3) – because our forefather Abraham was fearful, saying: ‘Perhaps I have a sin on my hands because I was an idol worshipper all those years?’ The Holy One blessed be He said to him: “The dew of your youth” – just as dew evaporates, so, too, your sins will evaporate; just as dew is a sign of blessing for the world, so, too, you are a sign of blessing for the world. That is what is written: “I said: Would that I had wings like a dove; I would fly away and come to rest” (Psalms 55:7). Why like a dove? Because all other birds, when they are weary, they rest on a stone or on a tree, but a dove, when it flies and grows weary, it folds one of its wings and flies with the other wing. “I would wander [nedod] far away” (Psalms 55:8) – movement after movement, wandering after wandering. “To repose in the wilderness, Selah” (Psalms 55:8) – it is preferable to repose in the wildernesses of the Land of Israel rather than to repose in the palaces outside the Land. And if you object that Abraham did not act immediately, and did not rejoice over the words of the Omnipresent, and [you ask] why did he not depart [at once]? It is because he had not yet been permitted, but once he was permitted: “Abram went as the Lord had spoken to him, and Lot went with him” (Genesis 12:4). Rabbi Levi said: When Abraham was traveling through Aram Naharayim and Aram Naḥor, he saw them eating, drinking, and reveling. He said: ‘Would that my portion not be in this land.’ When he reached the Promontory of Tyre, he saw them engaged in weeding at the time of weeding, hoeing at the time of hoeing, he said: ‘Would that my portion be in this land.’ The Holy One blessed be He said to him: “To your descendants I will give this land” (Genesis 12:7).”

p: אַךְ בְּרוֹב הַמְּקוֹמוֹת שֶׁנֶּזְכַּר טַל נִדְרָשׁ עַל טַלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא,
— However, in most scriptural contexts where dew is mentioned, it is expounded upon the supernal Dew of Atika Kadisha,
כְּמוֹ "מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם", דְּאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קמג עַמּוּד ב):
, — as in 'of the dew of heaven' (Genesis 27:28), of which it is stated (Zohar I, 143b):
"דָּא טַל עִלָּאָה דְּנָגֵיד מֵעַתִּיק יוֹמִין וְכוּלֵי";
— 'this is the supernal dew that flows down from the Ancient of Days, etc.';
וְכֵן "כִּי טַל אוֹרֹת טַלֶּךָ" נִדְרָשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (כְּתוּבּוֹת קיא עַמּוּד ב):
, — and likewise 'for your dew is as the dew of light' (Isaiah 26:19) is expounded in the Gemara (Ketubot 111b):
"כָּל הַמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּאוֹר תּוֹרָה, אוֹר תּוֹרָה מְחַיֵּיהוּ וְכוּלֵי",
— 'Whoever makes use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ טַל שֶׁעָתִיד בּוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת הַמֵּתִים (שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא שַׁבָּת פח עַמּוּד ב),
— and this is the dew with which the Holy One is destined to resurrect the dead (Shabbat 88b),
וְהוּא טַלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְנַז לְעַמְלֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— and it is the Dew of Atika derived from the Primordial Light that was hidden away for those who toil in the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ);
— as written (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach);
וּבַתִּקּוּנִים מַיְיתֵי בֶּאֱמֶת: "כָּל הָעוֹסֵק בְּטַל תּוֹרָה, טַל תּוֹרָה מְחַיֵּיהוּ".
, — and in the Tikkunim it is cited indeed: 'Whoever engages in the dew of Torah, the dew of Torah revives him.'

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Toldot 19:151 (I 143b): “The levels differ greatly. For concerning Jacob it is written, “May God give you of the dew of heaven.” This is the supernal dew flowing from the Ancient of Days, called the dew of heaven—the upper heaven—dew flowing through the level of heaven, and from there to the field of holy apples. “Of the fatness of the earth”: this is the supernal earth, the land of life. Concerning Esau it is written, “of the fatness of the earth”; concerning Jacob, “of the fatness of the earth” means the supernal land of life. He inherited the earth above and the heaven above, whereas Esau received the earth here below and the heaven here below. Jacob is high above; Esau is far below.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, Upon Completion of Talmud 2: “The Talmud begins with tractate Berakhot—with the mitzvot of reciting the Shema, prayer, and blessings, which are speech directly addressed to the blessed God and a clear recognition of His reality. This resembles “A maidservant saw at the sea,” and so forth: at the beginning, when a Jew begins to approach words of Torah, the blessed God opens a great light for him. As stated in Shabbat 88b: after their souls departed at the first utterance, the Holy One, blessed be He, brought out the dew with which He will revive the dead and restored them to life. The first utterance opens a great light; afterward He brings down dew, which dims the light. Dew appears only when there is no sunlight, as it says, “When the sun grew hot, it melted.” Yet with the blessed God, “Your dew is a dew of lights”: it is full of the light with which He will revive the dead. The explanation is that the Sages said, “Faithfulness”—this is the order Zeraim. Faith is needed when something is not clear to the eye and one must believe, as in “Your faithfulness at night”; by day it is called truth, because it is clear to the eye. Although a great light seems to open at the beginning, the blessed God has profound depths, light above light, beside which that first light is darkness. He wishes to raise a person ever higher. As soon as the person moves beyond the beginning, this light becomes familiar to him and returns to a state of darkness and faith.”

h: To you is the dew of your youth

p: וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶךָ", שֶׁהוּא טַלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא,
— And this is the meaning of 'To you is the dew of your youth,' which signifies the Dew of Atika,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט עַמּוּד ב):
— reflecting what they taught (Shabbat 89b):
"'אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים' – כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית וְעַד עַכְשָׁיו, כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ",
— “‘If your sins be as scarlet (kashanim)’—like these solar years (kashanim) that have been ordered and continuous since the six days of Creation until now, they shall become white as snow,”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה יִתְבָּרֵר
— meaning that through repentance out of supreme love it will become clarified
שֶׁכֵּן בְּמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית", שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "וַיֹּאמֶר", שֶׁהוּא שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן,
— that within the primordial utterance of 'Bereishit'—in which 'and He said' is not stated, it being the Intellect concealed from all conception—
כְּבָר הוּזְכַּר "תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ", שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה);
— there was already mentioned 'tohu va-vohu,' which hints at the deeds of the wicked (as written in Bereishit Rabbah);
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה הַמְּכֻוָּון: לִהְיוֹת בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא,
— meaning that this was the intentional divine design: that there be first darkness and subsequently light,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
— in order that the preeminence of light shine forth out of the darkness,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב, קפד עַמּוּד א):
— and reflecting that which is written (in the holy Zohar II, 184a):
"דְּהָא לֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא וְכוּלֵי",
— 'for there is no light except that which emerges from within the darkness, etc.,'
וְאָז "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" – שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
— and then 'they shall become white as snow'—transforming into absolute merits.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶךָ",
— And this is why it was said: 'To you is the dew of your youth,'
שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה הַמְּכֻוָּון מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִקּוֹדֶם הָאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנָה,
— that so was the deliberate intention of Hashem, blessed be He, that there precede those forty-eight initial years,
וְשֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יַכִּיר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ.
— and that only afterward Avraham our Father recognize his Creator.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "מָה הַטַּל פּוֹרֵחַ, אַף עֲוֹנוֹתֶיךָ פּוֹרְחִים",
— And this explains their statement: 'Just as the dew evaporates, so your sins evaporate,'
שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה מְסוּדָּר וּבָא מִמַּאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית" מֵעַתִּיקָא,
— for so it was prearranged and continuous from the primordial utterance of 'Bereishit' from Atika,
וְ"כַשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
— and 'they shall be white as snow,' becoming converted into merits.
"וּמָה הַטַּל סִימָן בְּרָכָה לָעוֹלָם, אַף אַתָּה סִימָן בְּרָכָה לָעוֹלָם".
,, — 'And just as the dew is a sign of blessing to the world, so too you are an omen of blessing to the world.'

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 1:4: “The foundation of Abraham our father’s level is that he was the first of the converts, as they said in Chagigah 3a. Only afterward, once Isaac was born and included within him, did he attain the name “Eitan the native,” to be like a native in Israel. The blessed God promised him, “Yours is the dew of your youth,” as stated in Bereishit Rabbah 39: “Might I bear sin?” and so forth. They interpreted “from the womb of the world”: in truth, Abraham our father too was holy from the womb and from the beginning of the world’s creation; only his beginning had been that of a convert. Afterward, however, he merited to reveal his root as the father of the world and the root of the entire Israelite people. He is the beginning of this lineage, the root of Israel, which can change what preceded it as well.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Tzidkat HaTzadik 40:1: “The essence of repentance is to reach the point at which God illuminates one’s eyes so that deliberate sins become merits. That is, one recognizes and understands that everything in which one sinned was also within the will of the blessed God, as our Sages said (Berakhot 31b), “Three verses …,” including “You turned their hearts backward” and “Whom I afflicted.” This follows the meaning of Divine knowledge and human choice explained by the Ari at the end of the book Arba Me’ot Shekel Kesef: both are true, each in its own domain. In the domain of choice there is no place for knowledge, and in the domain of knowledge there is truly no place for choice. When one attains this immense light, all one’s deliberate sins turn out not to have fallen outside the depth of the blessed God’s knowledge; He, His knowledge, and His will are all one. Since the blessed God willed it so, everything is a merit, and one attains the complete atonement of Yom Kippur. This is the secret of the goat sent to Azazel. If a person had performed this on his own initiative, he would have been an outright idolater: it would fall under “You shall have no other gods,” the foundation of all prohibitions and of all transgressions and departures from the blessed God’s will. But because the goat is sent by the blessed God’s will—He commands that it be sent there—it becomes a mitzvah rather than a transgression. Thus our Sages explained it (Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 46); see also Ramban on Acharei. We give a portion to Azazel, which is evil, because the blessed God commanded us to give it to him. Thus what would be a transgression becomes a mitzvah.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ha'azinu and Shabbat Shuvah 5: “When a person deepens his service, he then truly sees that all the places in which he stood very far from the blessed God are filled with light. This is what the Talmud teaches (Yoma 86b): when one returns from love, deliberate sins become merits. After the repentance by which he returns to God through great labor in His service, he truly sees that what had previously appeared to him as a position of great distance was filled with His will. This explains the midrash quoted above: Cain answered Adam, “I repented and reached a settlement,” whereupon Adam began, “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day.” For one attains this recognition fully on Shabbat. Then, when Shabbat comes, rest comes: one sees and explicitly recognizes that every place is full of light. As the Talmud says (Megillah 12b), “The seventh day was Shabbat”: the nations of the world eat and drink and begin indecent talk, while Israel begins songs and praises. My revered grandfather, of blessed memory, explained that the day itself causes this. On this day, as we say, “On the seventh day He rose and sat upon His throne of glory,” the nations say that this confirms their view that, God forbid, God has abandoned the earth, and they give themselves still greater license. Israel is different: on Shabbat it explicitly recognizes that all its power comes from the blessed God—even the power of repentance comes from the blessed God—and that the blessed God governs His world. It then explicitly recognizes that every place is filled with the light of the blessed God.”

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ:
— And this connects to what they stated in Midrash Tanchuma at the beginning of this parashah:
מַה שֶּׁיְּקַבֵּל עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם כְּשֶׁהוּא מְהַלֵּךְ וְכוּלֵי אָסוּר, אֶלָּא יַעֲמוֹד וְכוּלֵי,
— concerning whether one may accept the yoke of Heaven while walking, etc., it is forbidden; rather let him stand, etc.,
וּכְשֶׁמַּתְחִיל "וְאָהַבְתָּ" – רָצָה מְהַלֵּךְ וְכוּלֵי;
— and when he begins 'Ve-Ahavta'—if he wishes he may walk, etc.;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּדַּת כָּל הָאָבוֹת הָיְתָה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— meaning that the spiritual path of all the Patriarchs was active exertion in the service of Hashem,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צו עַמּוּד א):
— as written (Sanhedrin 96a):
"כְּשֶׁאֲנִי מְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר לְאַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁרָצוּ לְפָנַי כְּסוּסִים וְכוּלֵי",
— 'When I pay reward to Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov who ran before Me like horses, etc.,'
וּבִפְרָט אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה עִסְקוֹ קְדֻשַּׁת מִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאַהֲבָה וְהַזְּרִיזוּת,
— and especially Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, whose occupation was the sanctity of positive commandments from the root of Love and alacrity,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֻלִּין טז עַמּוּד א): "קְרָא זְרִיזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן",
— and as they said (Chullin 16a): 'Scripture comes to inform us of Avraham's alacrity,'
וְהוּא לֹא שָׁקַט וְלֹא נָח מִלְּהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— and he neither quieted down nor rested from toiling actively in deeds of divine service.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ: "לֶךְ לְךָ" – לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— And this is why it was said to him: 'Go for yourself'—to elevate your spiritual rung, as written in the holy Zohar,
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוֹלֵךְ תָּמִיד מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא בְּמִדָּתוֹ שֶׁהִיא הָאַהֲבָה,
— which signifies that he perpetually advance from level to level within his specific attribute of Love;
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְפָרָשַׁת "וְאָהַבְתָּ".
— and this corresponds to when one arrives at the paragraph of 'Ve-Ahavta.'
אֲבָל בְּיִחוּד ה', כְּשֶׁבָּא לְהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ שֶׁהֲוָיָ"ה אֶחָד,
— However, at the unification of Hashem, when reaching the realization that Hashem is One,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁאַתָּה הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא,
— which signifies that You are He after the world was created just as before it was created,
וְאָז צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת עוֹמֵד,
— then one must stand completely stationary,
שֶׁזֶּה מוֹרֶה עַל טַלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא שֶׁהַכֹּל מְסוּדָּר מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית;
— for this points to the Dew of Atika, wherein all is already ordered from the six days of Creation;
וְאָז יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם הָאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁהִכִּיר אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ,
— and then Hashem clarifies even the forty-eight years prior to his conscious recognition of his Creator,
שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
— as having been His divine will from the very Primordial Thought.
וּבֶאֱמֶת "יְהִי אוֹר" – זֶה אַבְרָהָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה.

paragraphs.text: Mesillas Yesharim 7:20–22: “Consider further: just as alacrity results from inward ardor, so inward ardor is also born of alacrity. When a person feels himself performing a mitzvah, as he hastens his outward movement, he thereby causes his inward movement to burn as well, and his longing and desire continue to grow stronger. But if he moves his limbs sluggishly, the movement of his spirit will also sink and be extinguished. Experience bears witness to this. You already know that what is most desired in serving the Creator, blessed be His Name, is the heart’s desire and the soul’s longing. This is what King David celebrates as his good portion, saying: “As a deer longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for You, God. My soul thirsts for God,” and so forth (Tehillim 42:2–3); “My soul longs and even pines for the courtyards of Hashem” (84:3); “My soul thirsts for You; my flesh longs for You” (63:2). For a person in whom this yearning does not burn as it should, good counsel is to act with alacrity by his own will, so that yearning will consequently arise naturally within him. For outward movement awakens the inward movement, and the outward is certainly more within his control than the inward. If he uses what is within his control, he will in time also acquire what is beyond his control: inward joy, desire, and yearning will arise within him through the force of willingly kindling his movement. This is what the prophet said: “Let us know; let us pursue the knowledge of Hashem” (Hoshea 6), and, “They shall walk after Hashem; He will roar like a lion” (ibid. 11).”

h: Avraham and the Descent of the Soul

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּרֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בְּסִטְרֵי תּוֹרָה מְרַמֵּז כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה עַל כָּל נְשָׁמָה;
— And in the holy Zohar at the beginning of this parashah in Sitrei Torah, the entire passage is allegorized unto every individual soul;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּן נֶאֱמַר לְכָל נְשָׁמָה,
— meaning that so it is addressed unto every soul,
אַךְ נִשְׁמַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, שֶׁהָיְתָה נְשָׁמָה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁיָּרְדָה לַגּוּף, נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ הַפָּסוּק.
— yet regarding the soul of Avraham our Father, which was the premier soul descending into a body, the verse is explicitly formulated.
וְאָמַר: "'וַיֹּאמֶר ה' אֶל אַבְרָם' – הָא נִשְׁמְתָא עִלָּאָה,
— And the Zohar states: “'And Hashem said unto Avram'—this is the supernal soul,
אַבָּא לְרוּחָא וְרָם לְגוּפָא",
— 'father (av) to the ruach, and exalted (ram) to the physical body,'
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב לְהַלָּן (עט עַמּוּד ב):
— and this is based on what is written later (79b):
דְּרוּחַ הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְהַיְינוּ אוֹתוֹ וָא"ו וְאִקְרֵי בֵּן;
— that Ruach is the Written Torah, represented by the letter Vav and termed 'Son';
וְשָׁם אָמַר: דְּהַנְּשָׁמָה אִתְעָרֵי לֶאֱינָשׁ בְּבִינָה, וְנִשְׁמְתָא לְנִשְׁמְתָא בְּחָכְמָה,
— and there it states that the Neshamah awakens a person in Binah, and the Neshamah of the Neshamah in Chokhmah,
וְהֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת יוֹ"ד הֵ"א שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם שֶׁמְּכוּנִים בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אַבָּא וְאִמָּא.
— these being the letters Yud-Hei of the Name which are termed Abba and Imma in the Zohar.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "אַבָּא לְרוּחָא", שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרָה דְּאִקְרֵי בֵּן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קכג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב),
— And this is why it says 'father to the ruach,' which is Torah titled Son (Zohar III, 123b),
"וְרָם לְגוּפָא", שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַגּוּף, וְהוּא עִם מַדְרֵגוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ חַיּוּת הַגּוּף שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם), כְּנֶגְדּוֹ נִקְרָא "רָם".
— 'and exalted to the body,' for facing the body and the rungs of Nefesh (bodily vitality) representing the performance of mitzvot, it is titled exalted (ram).

h: The Soul’s Journey into the Body

p: וְאָמַר סֵדֶר בִּיאַת הַנְּשָׁמָה:
— And the Zohar delineates the order of the soul's descent:
"מֵאַרְצְךָ" – דָּא גִּנְתָא דְעֵדֶן,
— “‘From your land’—this is the Garden of Eden,”
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, כו עַמּוּד א):
— which is based on what is written in the holy Zohar (I, 26a):
"מֵעֵדֶן – דָּא אִמָּא עִלָּאָה", וְהַנְּשָׁמָה מִבִּינָה כָּאָמוּר.
— “‘From Eden’—this is the Supernal Mother (Imma),” the soul emanating from Binah as noted.
וְאַף דְּגַן שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה, וְכָאן אָמַר: "דָּא גִּנְתָא דְעֵדֶן",
— And although 'Garden' normally refers to the lower Shechinah, while here it says 'this is the Garden of Eden,'
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, קפב עַמּוּד ב):
— it is according to what is written in the holy Zohar (III, 182b):
הַאי עֵדֶן תַּתָּאָה אִקְרֵי גַּן לְעֵדֶן דִּלְעֵילָא, וְהַאי גַּן אִקְרֵי עֵדֶן לְגַן דִּלְתַתָּא,
— this lower Eden is called a garden relative to the supernal Eden, and this garden is called Eden relative to the lower garden,
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "דָּא גִּנְתָא דְעֵדֶן",
— and this is why it says 'this is the Garden of Eden,'
וְהַיְינוּ: "מֵאַרְצְךָ" הוּא עֵדֶן תַּתָּאָה דְּאִקְרֵי גַּן לְעֵדֶן דִּלְעֵילָא.
— meaning 'from your land' is the lower Eden that is termed a garden to the higher Eden.
"וּמִמּוֹלַדְתְּךָ" – דָּא אִילָנָא דְחַיֵּי, וְהוּא תִּפְאֶרֶת.
— ‘And from your birthplace’—this is the Tree of Life, which is Tiferet.
"וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ" – דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא,
— ‘And from your father's house’—this is the Shechinah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ: "אָבִיךָ – דָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא", וּבֵית אָבִיךָ הַיְינוּ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל;
— and as written subsequently: 'your father'—this is the Holy One, and your father's house is Knesset Yisrael;
וְכֵן הַגִּרְסָא: "וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ – תְּרֵיסַר תְּחוּמִין שִׁבְטִין עִלָּאִין", הַכֹּל אֶחָד,
— and so is the variant textual reading: 'and from your father's house—twelve boundaries of supernal tribes,' all being one unified concept,
דִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים הַיְינוּ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— since the twelve tribes constitute Knesset Yisrael.
"אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ" – דָּא אִיהוּ הַאי עַלְמָא, וְהַיְינוּ הַגּוּף.
— ‘Unto the land that I will show you’—this is this physical world, meaning the human body.

p: וְכֵן סֵדֶר כָּל נְשָׁמָה שֶׁיּוֹרֶדֶת לַגּוּף הוּא מִכָּל הַקְּדוּשׁוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרוֹת,
— And such is the trajectory of every soul descending into the body—traversing all these aforementioned sanctities;
אַךְ אַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב: "וַיֵּלֶךְ אִתּוֹ לוֹט",
— yet afterward it is written: 'And Lot went with him' (Genesis 12:4),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ לְהַלָּן:
— and as the holy Zohar expounds further:
"דָּא אִיהוּ נָחָשׁ דְּאִתְלַטְיָא וְאִתְלַטְיָא עַלְמָא בְּגִינֵיהּ",
— 'this is the primordial serpent that was cursed (itlatya) and on whose account the world was cursed,'
וּמִזֶּה נִסְתָּעֵף הָאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנָה.
— and from this branched forth the forty-eight years before Avraham recognized his Creator.
וְכֵן בְּכָל אָדָם, הַנְּשָׁמָה יוֹרֶדֶת לַגּוּף בְּכָל הַקְּדוּשׁוֹת,
— And so too with every person: the soul descends into the body invested with all holy degrees,
רַק הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוֹלֵךְ עִמָּהּ תֵּיכֶף,
— only that the evil inclination accompanies it immediately,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו",
— as is stated: 'For the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth' (Genesis 8:21),
וְנִדְרָשׁ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (פֶּרֶק ג דִּבְרָכוֹת הֲלָכָה ה) וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה לד):
— and expounded in the Yerushalmi (Berakhot 3:5) and Bereishit Rabbah (34):
"מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁהוּא נִנְעָר לָצֵאת מִמְּעֵי אִמּוֹ".
— 'from the moment he is stirred (nin'ar) to emerge from his mother's womb.'
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: "דְּהָא מִתְּרֵיסַר שְׁנִין וּלְעֵילָא נִשְׁמְתָא אִתְעָרַת לְמִפְלַח פּוּלְחָנָא וְכוּלֵי";
— And afterward it states: 'for from twelve years and upward the holy soul is awakened to serve the divine service, etc.';
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁמְּתַקֵּן הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה,
— and subsequently when one rectifies all through repentance,
אוֹמֵר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶךָ",
— Hashem, blessed be He, proclaims to him: 'To you is the dew of your youth,'
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלָיו בִּימֵי יַלְדוּתוֹ כַּטַּל הַפּוֹרֵחַ,
— showing that whatever passed over him in the days of his youth is like evaporating dew,
שֶׁמְּבָרֵר אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִטַּלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא
— which Hashem refines through the supernal Dew of Atika,
שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה מְסוּדָּר מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית לִהְיוֹת בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא,
— demonstrating that so it was preordained from the six days of Creation to be first darkness and then light,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאוֹר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
— so that the light attain its consummate perfection,
דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא כָּאָמוּר.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Shabbat 1: “If a person always stood in clarity like the heavens, his service would not be counted as something he attained through the labor of his hands. Therefore the blessed God concealed His way, and a person does not always stand in clarity like the heavens. For this reason He gave His people Israel Torah and mitzvot. Through bearing Torah and mitzvot—as the Talmud says, “Our leaders are in Torah and laden with mitzvot”—a person can become refined and stand in clarity as before, but now through his service. This is the meaning of “The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to grant merit to Israel; therefore He gave them abundant Torah and mitzvot”: through Torah and mitzvot a person can become refined and stand in clarity before the blessed God. This also occurred at the giving of the Torah. The angels again protested, “How mighty is Your name throughout the earth; place Your majesty upon the heavens.” They were saying that, since the blessed God wished to refine creation, He could refine it all at once so that it would always stand like the heavens, without any need for Torah and mitzvot. Moses answered them, “Do you have an evil inclination?” Although they always stand in tremendous clarity, their service cannot be called the labor of their hands. The blessed God’s present will is that Israel’s service should come through Torah and mitzvot and be attributed to them. As it says, “The word He commanded for a thousand generations,” which the Midrash applies to the giving of the Torah: it would have been fitting for the Torah to be given after a thousand generations, so why was it given after twenty-six generations? Because they were upright, and so forth. Had He given it after a thousand generations, everything would have come from the blessed God’s side, and Torah would have been kept of necessity, with no choice. The blessed God wished to benefit His creatures and to attribute the service to the person. He therefore brought it forward to the twenty-sixth generation, so that they would have choice: a person would choose good and reject evil, and this would be called the labor of his hands.”

h: Shabbat and the Transformation of Past Deeds

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת בִּסְעוּדָתָא דְעַתִּיקָא
— And on Shabbat at the feast of Atika Kadisha,
יָכוֹל הָאָדָם לִזְכּוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
— a person can merit to rectify all his past deeds so that they convert into merits,
כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וְכוּלֵי;
— like those solar years that are prearranged, etc.;
וְזֶה מִקְּדֻשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לְטַלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא.
— and this flows from the sanctity of Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, who merited the Dew of Atika.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Second Day of Pesach 7:2: “Dew signifies the essential will stripped of any garment. Therefore the Talmud says that dew is not withheld: rain signifies the will clothed in a material garment from the standpoint of human perception, whereas dew has no garment at all. It is the clarity of the will as it is in its Divine source, the light of life that flows secretly into everything in the world. It is that which proceeds from God’s mouth, giving life and existence to all things. Therefore, in Isaac’s blessing, “You are mighty,” we mention “He brings down the dew.” Dew signifies this will that flows life into all things, for in truth there is no life in the world except the life flowing from this will. This too is Isaac’s quality of might: to illuminate in this world that there is judgment and a Judge—that no creature possesses any independent power, but must receive the power of life anew from the blessed God at every moment. We therefore speak of the resurrection of the dead in Isaac’s blessing. The dew with which the Holy One, blessed be He, will revive the dead is awakened through Isaac’s quality: through him, recognition is awakened in all things that all their life comes only from the Divine will flowing within them. Dew signifies that will, wholly without human action. Yet all His desire is that the flow from this dew be recognizable also in this world, within the perception of this world and in all actions. He therefore arranged for there to be weekday dew: on weekdays, the flow comes through the servant Metatron, as explained in the holy Zohar, to indicate that it is clothed and descends through an intermediary, through human action. On weekdays a person receives the flow through his actions, although his essential life always comes from what proceeds from God’s mouth, which has no garment. On weekdays, however, this light is clothed and received through various screens and garments. On Shabbat this light is explicitly recognizable: there is no active power except the blessed God alone and no other power in the world. All human activity then rests, and the light of this dew is explicitly recognizable. A person understands that he is nourished only from the very supernal light, from His simple will, with no action on his own part at all.”
